title: Choose the visual world — How Votes Flow
question: The roll assigned The Arena Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Arena Board
options.lineage: stadium scoreboards and broadcast score bugs
options.thesis: The election as a live game: four teams, three periods, first lane to 51 wins — and you watch the points change hands.
options.viewport: Four huge score lanes over a buzzer line at 51, the 100 tokens massed courtside below; one button tips off Round 1.
options.risk: A sports frame can read as trivializing in sober civic contexts; it must stay warm playground-tournament, not bloodsport.

raised.raise: One board, two grips — editing the lineup happens on the same arena board you watch, never a separate setup screen.
The strike — an eliminated team is killed by one bold diagonal stripe that reads at any size, on any screen.
Leader-line counts — every transfer stream states its own number, pinned where it happens, so no motion goes unlabeled.

options.label: Election Night
options.lineage: TV election-night studio boards and race-call graphics
options.thesis: The count as election-night coverage: races tightening on a dark studio wall, calls checked, the night wearing on.
options.viewport: A dark studio wall of four race panels with call slots and a 51% bar; tokens wait as a paper-stack column by the desk.
options.risk: The direction most runs in this category would land on — familiar and effective, least distinctive.

options.label: Seven-Segment Totem
options.lineage: alarm clocks, gas-price totems, microwave panels
options.thesis: Every count as an eight-cell LED mask: digits die and ignite, nothing ever slides.
options.viewport: A tower of four giant segment readouts with ghost cells behind, transfers as digits flickering upward.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: tallies become segment masks and eliminations become digits dying; it counts sharply but cannot carry the flow-and-cheer narrative.
options.risk: Reads as a clock, not a contest, when the ghost cells do all the talking.

options.label: The Midnight Interchange
options.lineage: enamel transit diagrams, four colored lines
options.thesis: Every ballot a journey: your vote rides a colored line and re-routes at the interchange when its line is suspended.
options.viewport: Four route lines crossing at one interchange, ballots as tokens riding lines that get suspended one by one.
options.case: Fuses startlingly well: vote transfer IS a re-route at an interchange, and four colorblind-safe line inks are built in; loses on live totals and threshold drama, which maps do not natively show.
options.risk: Implies a geography the election doesn't have; totals live in a legend instead of the world.

options.label: The Civic Poster
options.thesis: Each round as a silkscreen poster plane: one imperative in blocky caps, four flat inks, the count printed in sunlight.
options.viewport: A stacked-plane scene with a caption bar — ROUND 2: MAYA IS OUT — and the tallies printed into the sky.
options.case: Fuses warmly: WPA is literally civic-education poster lineage and the caption bar is a perfect round-narrator; loses because static planes fight a live-updating counter.
options.risk: Charm without liveness — a poster celebrates a result, it doesn't count one.

options.label: The Card Stack
options.case: Fuses poorly: one-bit monochrome strains the four-color candidate coding a party-neutral cast needs; nostalgia narrows the audience.
options.kept: Browse and author as one object — editing in place.

options.label: Stockroom Quotes
options.lineage: industrial streetwear, hazard stripes, zip-tie tags
options.case: Fuses poorly: stockroom cool isn't civic warmth, and quoted labels don't carry counting.
options.kept: One unambiguous strike device for eliminated states.

options.label: The Tension Column
options.lineage: tensegrity sculpture, carbon rods and red cord
options.case: Fuses poorly: abstract physics adds a translation layer between the visitor and a civic process.
options.kept: Leader-line annotations pinned to every node.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: An explainer headline over an editable ballot card and a results sankey.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other voting explainer by design.
